subject: Communication
title: BATNA: Your Best Alternative
description: Learn BATNA: Your Best Alternative in one minute.

hook.text: She walked into the salary negotiation knowing exactly what she'd do if they said no. That changed everything.

buildup.text: BATNA — Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — is the most powerful concept in negotiation theory.

discovery.text: Your BATNA is your plan B. Knowing it gives you confidence to walk away from bad deals and hold firm on fair ones.

twist.text: The party with the better BATNA has more power — regardless of authority, title, or resources.

climax.text: Improving your BATNA before negotiating is often more effective than improving your arguments during negotiation.

punchline.text: Power in negotiation isn't about dominance. It's about options.

quiz.question: What does BATNA stand for?
options: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement
Basic Agreement Terms and Necessities Assessment

details.summary: BATNA stands for Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement, the strongest option you have if talks fail. Knowing your BATNA gives you power and clarity: you should never accept a deal worse than your alternative. A strong BATNA lets you negotiate from confidence.
details.whyItMatters: Your BATNA determines your walk-away point. Without knowing it, you negotiate blind and risk accepting bad outcomes out of desperation.
takeaways: BATNA is your best option if the negotiation fails
A strong BATNA increases your negotiating power
Never accept an offer worse than your BATNA

faq.question: How do you strengthen a weak BATNA?
faq.answer: Develop multiple alternatives before entering negotiations. Research other options, build new relationships, and improve your position independently. The more viable alternatives you create, the less dependent you are on any single negotiation outcome.

faq.question: Should you reveal your BATNA to the other side?
faq.answer: Only when it strengthens your position. If your BATNA is strong, hinting at it can motivate the other party to offer better terms. If it is weak, revealing it gives them leverage. Strategic ambiguity about alternatives is often the wisest approach.
